title: Composite-threshold automatic fallback & progressive circuit-breaker strategy for routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Several incidents and load tests showed that single-metric triggers (e.g., >X 429s or >Y p95 latency) either fire too late or oscillate, causing unnecessary failovers or downstream overload. We need a robust, production-safe automatic fallback and circuit-breaker system that considers multiple signals (429 spikes, client/server timeout rates, error-rate, latency percentiles) with hysteresis, progressive degradation, and tenant/route/region scoping.

Goal: Implement a composite-threshold engine and progressive circuit-breaker policies surfaced in the routing layer that: (1) detect degraded health quickly, (2) avoid flip-flopping via cooldowns and weighted signals, (3) support scoped activation (route/model/region/tier), and (4) provide observable, reversible actions (fallback to compatible model variants, shift to lower tier, redirect region, or serve cached prefix).
acceptance_criteria: Composite triggers evaluate at configurable windows (10s, 1m, 5m) and combine weighted signals (429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate, p95 latency) to produce a single health score per route/region/tenant.

When score crosses 'degraded' threshold, routing begins progressive fallback: small percentage of traffic (5%) diverted to fallback model variant for 1 minute, then ramp to 25%/60s, then 100% if sustained.

Circuit breaker opens if sustained error/timeout rate above threshold for configured window; when open, route uses next-best compatible model variant or region fallback and schedules periodic probe requests.
Cooldown and hysteresis parameters prevent oscillation: minimum open time, exponential backoff on retries, and manual override via Console rollouts.
Dashboard and alerting: per-route health score, triggers fired, fallback percentages, and impact on token-cost/latency; SLO degradations are visible in Console and linked in alerts.
Automated tests: unit tests for threshold logic, integration E2E load tests simulating 429/timeouts, and a staging canary rollout validating progressive fallback behavior.
design_decisions: Use a rolling-window counter architecture in the routing proxy (envoy filter) to compute per-route per-region metrics; avoid centralized store for low-latency decisions.
Health score is a weighted sum: 40% p95 latency z-score, 30% 429 rate, 20% timeout rate, 10% 5xx rate. Weights are config-driven per project/tier.
Progressive fallback implemented as percent-based traffic steering (TrafficSplit) rather than immediate full failover to allow live validation and minimize user-visible errors.
Probes are synthetic requests that validate model variant compatibility and response correctness before closing breakers. Probe cadence limited to avoid added load.
Fallback variants include: quantized model variant (lower resource), regional replica, and cached-prefix responder. Selector order is configured by policy and customer tier.
tradeoffs: Local counters in proxies are fast but approximate (inconsistent across nodes); we accept eventual consistency in exchange for sub-100ms decision latency.
Weighted composite score gives flexibility but increases tuning complexity; we will ship sane defaults and expose tuning knobs in Console for advanced users.
Progressive percentages reduce risk but add implementation complexity in routing layer (requires distributed traffic split support).
Probing increases cluster traffic slightly; we limit probe volume and use lightweight probes to minimize cost.
rollout_plan: Week 1 (staging): Feature flag behind 'composite-fallback' and 'progressive-breaker' in staging region; run synthetic load tests and compare behavior vs current simplistic rule-based system.
Week 2 (canary): Enable on 5% of hostnames in prod traffic for non-critical tiers (internal customers) with additional logging; run burn-in for 72h.
Week 3 (gradual): Expand to 25% then 100% for P2/P3 traffic while P0/P1 remain conservative; expose Console controls for manual overrides and per-customer policies.
Observability: release dashboards and alerts before broader rollout; add audit log entries for every automated fallback decision.
metrics_to_monitor: Trigger events: fallback-start, fallback-step-up, circuit-open, circuit-close, probe-failure
Traffic split percentages to fallback variants
SLO violation rate and user-visible error rate during fallback windows
